title: Protocol for determining zinc-dependent β cell-selective small-molecule delivery in mouse pancreas
protocol: Prepare frozen mouse pancreas sections.
Label plastic blocks and fill with OCT at 20°C–24°C.
Avoid introducing air bubbles during filling.
Have dry ice ready in an insulated container.
Dissect out mouse pancreas.
Euthanize the mouse by anesthetizing it with isoflurane overdose, then performing cervical dislocation.
Open the body cavity and cut the pancreas away from the spleen and duodenum.
Take special care to include the islet rich pancreatic tail in the dissection.
Place the dissected pancreas in OCT.
Use forceps to shape the pancreas into a dense ball.
Submerge the shaped pancreas fully in OCT.
Place the mold containing the OCT and pancreas on dry ice.
Do not fix the tissue at any stage, as TSQ/Zn2+ staining will be removed.
Transfer to −80°C for storage or continue with tissue sectioning.
Have clear slides at 20°C–24°C next to a cryostat for section mounting.
Prepare dry ice for storing completed slides.
Set cryostat blade to cut 10 μm sections.
Mount frozen block in cryostat.
Cut into the block until the pancreas is included on sections.
Place intact pancreatic sections on (+)-charged slides.
Store sections on dry ice while cutting, or place directly at −80°C.
Prepare at least 8 sections for testing individual compounds.
Prepare at least 2 sections for control treatments.
Prepare phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Dilute Nuclear Green (DCS-1) in PBS to achieve a final concentration of 1 μM.
Dilute TSQ to 10 μM in the DCS-1 staining solution.
Make at least 500 μL of each compound solution to be tested.
Use DCS-1 solution to dilute experimental compounds for testing.
Test experimental compounds at concentrations ranging from 500 μM to 1 μM.
Dilute TPEN to 500 μM in the DCS-1 solution as a positive control.
Make a vehicle control by preparing a 5% solution of DMSO in DCS-1 solution.
Bring tissue sections to a temperature range of 20°C–24°C.
Wash tissue sections by dipping them in PBS.
Carefully dry off excess liquid from the sections using a lint-free wipe.
Demarcate the pancreas on the section using a hydrophobic marker in a small circle.
Add the TSQ-containing staining solution (50 μL) to the section.
Incubate the section with the TSQ staining solution for 5 minutes, covered with aluminum foil.
Remove the TSQ staining solution with a pipette without disturbing the tissue.
Pipette the experimental or control compound solution (50 μL) onto the TSQ-stained section.
Incubate the section with the experimental or control compound solution for 5 minutes, covered with aluminum foil.
Remove the experimental or control compound solution and replace it with 100 μL PBS per tissue sample.
Determine islet TSQ fluorescence.
Place slides on a fluorescent microscope at 10–20× magnification.
Find islets by locating areas with sparse nuclei as seen in the green channel.
Obtain microscope images to capture green fluorescence (Excitation 503 nm, Emission 526 nm).
Capture blue fluorescence (Excitation 370 nm, Emission 495 nm).
Capture at least 3 images at 20× magnification of different islets on every section.
Repeat the above staining protocol for every experimental compound concentration.
Quantify and plot islet fluorescence using Photoshop or equivalent software.
Identify islets in the green channel.
Demarcate areas of interest using the elliptical marquee tool.
Record the median fluorescent intensity of the identified region(s) in the blue channel.
Move the marquee tool to a non-islet area and record blue median fluorescence.
Calculate the ratio of islet to exocrine median fluorescence in the blue (TSQ) channel for all islets imaged.
Normalize islet/exocrine fluorescence ratio to 0% (TPEN-treated) and 100% (DMSO-treated).
Plot the normalized fluorescence according to experimental compound treatment concentration using Prism or equivalent software.
Fit the dilution data to a 4-parameter inhibition curve to obtain the 4 parameter values of Top, Bottom, IC50, and nH.
Obtain islets and exocrine pancreas from mice.
Euthanize mice by isoflurane overdose followed by cervical dislocation.
Isolate islets from pancreata using bile duct-based collagenase A perfusion.
Extract isolated tissues and separate using histopaque centrifugation.
Collect and suspend isolated islets in low glucose DMEM with 1× penicillin-streptomycin and 10% fetal bovine serum.
Collect and suspend pelleted exocrine tissue in low glucose DMEM with 1× penicillin-streptomycin and 10% fetal bovine serum.
Keep pelleted exocrine tissue cold on ice during the islet extraction process.
Quantify protein in handpicked islets and exocrine tissue.
Spin down an aliquot of islets and resuspend in PBS, then lyse by at least 3 freeze/thaw cycles.
Use a fraction of the collected tissues to quantify total islet and exocrine protein using DC Protein Assay or equivalent assay.
Split islet and exocrine tissue into PCR tubes at equivalent protein concentrations (0.1–0.5 μg/μL).
Dilute samples to 10 μL per condition (i.e., 1–5 μg).
Add TPEN (1 mM final concentration) or vehicle (DMSO) to conditions.
Incubate for 5 minutes in thermal cycler at 37°C.
Add test compounds in media (recommended concentration of 10 μM).
Include the addition of a non-chelating compound [10 μM] for normalizing zinc-dependent drug accumulation.
Perform experiment in quadruplicate, preferably with n=6–12 samples.
Include TSQ (10 μM)-treated islets and exocrine tissue as a positive control.
Incubate islets and exocrine tissue in a thermal cycler for 30 min at 37°C.
Place samples on ice (0°C).
Rapidly add 50 μL PBS to the samples.
Spin down samples (<20 s, ≤2,000 × g).
Remove PBS from the samples.
Repeat the wash step with another 50 μL PBS.
After second wash, suspend tissues in 20 μL PBS total.
Freeze suspended tissues at −20°C.
Prepare a calibration curve with compounds of interest from 50 μM down to 1 nM in MeOH, water, or MeCN.
Dilute islet and exocrine pancreas assay samples, as well as all standards in the calibration curve, 1:2 in 50% MeCN/50% water with 0.1% formic acid.
Centrifuge all diluted samples.
Place supernatant free of particulate into LC-MS/MS plates or vials.
If particulate remains, adjust MeCN/water mix and/or dilute further.
Run standard curves and samples over LC-MS/MS using a gradient of MeCN and water.
Start with a gradient of 95% water→40% water→50% water→95% water over 4–6 min.
If analyte peaks appear at the beginning or end of the elution, adjust gradient or change solvents.
Quantify each analyte peak according to its peak area in the standard curve.
Plot compound accumulation (nmol/g protein) and ratio to non-chelator in sample for islets and exocrine tissue.
Obtain islets from rats.
Euthanize Sprague-Dawley (250 g) rats using isoflurane overdose followed by cervical dislocation.
Isolate islets from pancreata using bile duct-based collagenase A perfusion followed by tissue extraction and histopaque centrifugation as described.
Collect and suspend isolated islets in low glucose DMEM with 1× penicillin-streptomycin and 10% fetal bovine serum.
Culture suspended islets in a tissue culture incubator for 12–16 h.
Treat 384-well black fluorescence cell culture plates with 804-G cell conditioned medium (50 μL per well).
Place treated plates in a cell culture incubator at 37°C for 12–16 h.
Disperse islets into single cells.
Collect isolated islets in a 50 mL conical tube and centrifuge at 197 × g for 5 min.
Warm Trypsin-EDTA and low glucose DMEM with 10% FBS and 1× penicillin-streptomycin to 37°C.
Carefully remove supernatant using a 1 mL aspirating pipet with a 200 μL pipet tip on the end.
Wash cells with PBS (30 mL), centrifuge at 197 × g for 5 min.
Remove supernatant carefully as in step 9c.
Suspend islet pellet in pre-warmed Trypsin-EDTA (250 μL per rat) and place at 37°C for 5 min.
Pipette up and down with a 1,000 μL pipet 25 times, then place at 37°C for another 5 min.
Pipette up and down with a 200 μL pipet 30 times and place at 37°C for an additional 5 min.
Pipette up and down with a 200 μL pipet 30 times. If visible chunks of islets remain, add more trypsin and repeat steps 9e–9h.
Place digested islets on ice.
Count a 1:10 dilution of digested islets using a hemocytometer.
Repeat count for precision using a fresh 1:10 dilution of digested islets.
Calculate the number of wells that can be plated based on cell density requirements.
Dilute trypsinized cells in low glucose DMEM with 10% FBS and 1× penicillin-streptomycin to a final volume of 60 μL/well.
Plate the cells in the coated 384-well cell culture plates, avoiding edge wells for consistency.
Culture cells for 48 h at 37°C to allow attachment.
Prepare concentrated stock solutions of experimental compounds (10 mM in DMSO).
Include a positive control replication-inducing compound such as GNF-4877 or OTS-167.
Dilute compounds in media to 3× the desired final concentration for treatment solutions.
Include at least 6 DMSO-treated wells to establish a baseline replication rate.
Perform a partial media exchange by adding 50 μL per well.
Remove 70 μL from each well to leave a final volume of 40 μL.
Treat cells with 20 μL of the prepared β cell replication-stimulating compound or DMSO solutions.
Incubate at 37°C for 48–72 hours.
Remove culture media by inverting and forcefully decanting the tissue culture plate.
Fix cells using 8% PFA (60 μL/well) for 20 minutes.
Replace PFA with PBS (100 μL/well).
Freshly prepare antigen retrieval solution by diluting 0.15 M sodium citrate pH 6.0 at a 1:20 dilution in formamide.
Decant PBS solution from the wells.
Immediately add antigen retrieval solution (70 μL/well) and heat at 70°C for 45 minutes using a water bath positioned to cover the skirt of the plate without submerging it.
Place a heavy object on top of the plate during heating to prevent bowing/deformation.
Remove from water bath and allow the plate to cool (15 minutes at 20°C–24°C).
Wash wells with PBS twice (100 μL/well).
Apply blocking solution (6.25% donkey serum, 0.3% Tx-100 in PBS; 50 μL/well) for 30 minutes at 20°C–24°C.
Prepare antibody dilution solution by diluting the blocking solution 1:5 in PBS.
Decant blocking solution.
Add primary antibodies in antibody dilution solution (40–50 μL/well).
Incubate at 4°C for 12–16 hours.
Decant primary antibody solution.
Wash twice with PBS (100 μL/well).
Add secondary antibodies in antibody dilution solution (40–50 μL/well).
Cover the plate with aluminum foil.
Incubate at 20°C–24°C for 1 hour.
Wash twice with PBS (100 μL/well).
Treat with Hoechst 33342 staining solution (50 μL/well) for 20 minutes.
Remove Hoechst staining solution.
Replace with 100 μL PBS.
Define parameters to exclude fibroblasts.
Select cells of interest by applying a nuclear (Hoechst) staining intensity threshold.
Apply a maximum value for nuclear size since islet endocrine cells have smaller nuclei than fibroblasts.
Define replication events by the presence of Ki-67-positive staining in β cells or non-β cells.
Define β cell events based on insulin and/or PDX-1 co-staining.
Acquire images (70 fields/well) and quantify the frequency of replication events.
Determine the average basal (DMSO-treated) β cell and non-β cell replication rates using the provided formulas.
Determine the compound-induced replication rates for both β cell and non-β cell populations.
Determine the fold replication induced by each treatment by dividing the induced replication rate by the average basal replication rate.
Determine selectivity ratio by dividing the fold replication induced in β cells by the fold replication induced in non-β cells.
